classification.difficultyReason: Follow the explicit derivative-to-gradient-to-line scaffold, select the stated intercepts, and convert the negative tangent y-intercept into a positive triangle height. These are routine linked procedures; the supplied derivative and area constrain the work.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $y=2\sin^2 x$ has derivative $y'=4\sin x\cos x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the gradients of the tangent and normal to $y=2\sin^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.worked:
At $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\begin{align*}y'&=4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\\&=4\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\\&=2.\end{align*}$$
Gradient of tangent $=2$.

Gradient of normal $=-\frac{1}{2}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the equations of the tangent and normal to $y=2\sin^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Suppose that the normal meets the $x$-axis at $P$, the tangent meets the $y$-axis at $Q$ and $O$ is the origin. Show that $\triangle OPQ$ has area $\frac{(\pi+8)(\pi-2)}{16}$ units$^2$.

answer.worked:
The normal $x+2y=\frac{\pi}{4}+2$ meets the $x$-axis where $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\pi}{4}+2,\\P&=\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+2,0\right).\end{align*}$$
The tangent $2x-y=\frac{\pi}{2}-1$ meets the $y$-axis where $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=1-\frac{\pi}{2},\\Q&=\left(0,1-\frac{\pi}{2}\right).\end{align*}$$
Since the coordinate axes are perpendicular and $\pi>2$,
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OPQ)&=\frac12|OP||OQ|\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+2\right)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi+8}{4}\right)\left(\frac{\pi-2}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{(\pi+8)(\pi-2)}{16}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
